headlines: MIAMI-DADE VOTERS DECIDE KEY MUNICIPAL RACES ACROSS 22 CITIES
INCUMBENTS OUSTED ACROSS MIAMI-DADE IN TUESDAY ELECTIONS
SEE HOW YOUR MIAMI-DADE HOMETOWN VOTED ON TUESDAY
draft.article:
Voters across 22 Miami-Dade County municipalities decided local leadership and dozens of ballot measures on Tuesday.

Incumbents faced steep challenges. El Portal Mayor Omarr Nickerson lost his race, and Coral Gables Commissioner Melissa Castro fell short by 121 votes. Key Biscayne and Medley incumbents also lost, while a razor-thin 16-vote margin in Doral triggered an automatic recount for Council Member Maureen Porras.

Other leaders held ground. Aventura Mayor Howard Weinberg secured reelection with 79 percent, and Coral Gables Mayor Vince Lago earned his final term with 57 percent. Countywide, voters passed 37 of 48 referendums. Runoffs will stretch from November 17 into December.

headlines: MIAMI BEACH VOTERS REJECT 2132 LEASE EXTENSION FOR LUXURY OFFICES
SOUTH BEACH RESIDENTS BLOCK MASSIVE OFFICE EXPANSION PLAN
LOCALS PROTECT SOUTH BEACH LAND FROM CENTURY LONG LEASE DEAL
draft.article: Miami Beach voters decided against a proposal on Tuesday that would have extended a city land lease until 2132 for an ultra-luxury office building at 1691 Michigan Avenue. Nearly 63 percent of voters rejected the referendum involving developer RK Rivani LLC, located just off Lincoln Road. The decision halts 47,000 square feet of planned new development, which included a 50 million dollar upgrade with a restaurant, extra offices, and rooftop padel courts. Onsite parking will remain at 700 spaces instead of shrinking to 475. The property, home to Playboy headquarters, will keep its current lease running through 2052, with options through 2092.

headlines: ONE DEAD, TWO INJURED IN KEY BISCAYNE HELICOPTER CRASH

draft.article: A helicopter crash off Key Biscayne left one person dead and two others seriously injured Wednesday around 11:30 a.m. The aircraft went down in the waters near Bill Baggs State Park. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews rushed to the scene and airlifted the two injured survivors directly to Ryder Trauma Center at Jackson Memorial Hospital. The Coast Guard confirmed that one individual died in the incident. Federal officials from the National Transportation Safety Board have launched an investigation into the crash. Authorities identified the downed aircraft as a Robinson R44 II helicopter registered to Global Aerials Inc.
